hypothesis: Reproduce the official FM baseline under the harness contract.
Replace pointwise logloss with within-user BPR so training directly improves positive-negative ordering while cancelling metric-irrelevant user-constant effects.
expected_delta_basis: The card projects 0.002–0.010, Fact 7 confirms many discriminative users, and project calibration maps a nominal 0.006 ranking-loss gain to about +0.0022.

rejected_alternative.reason: It has comparable expected gain but requires more segment-normalization code, making BPR the cheaper ranking-aligned first probe.

change_summary: Replace pointwise logloss updates with pure within-user BPR, precomputing mixed-user positive/negative pools and sampling one same-user negative per positive each epoch.

reasons: No leakage: outcomes are used only as training targets/pair labels or validation evaluation labels; scored-row features remain legal.
Contract and scope are satisfied: deterministic same-user BPR, capped by SMOKE_EPOCHS, linear preprocessing, and preserved prediction order.

hypothesis: Exponentially downweight early training rows so item and interaction estimates emphasize the late-April regime that most closely matches validation and hidden test.
expected_delta_basis: The card range is 0.001–0.006, while Fact 5 shows severe volume and label drift plus a measured −0.007 FM valid-to-test gap, supporting a lower-third estimate near +0.002.

rejected_alternative.reason: The peaked curve supports scheduling, but its 0.000–0.003 range is lower and early stopping already preserves the best epoch.

change_summary: Apply normalized exponential recency weights with a fixed seven-day half-life to pointwise training gradients and loss diagnostics.

reasons: No leakage or test access; validation labels are used only for evaluation.
The fixed seven-day weighting is scoped, deterministic, smoke-capped, and its +0.002 expectation is plausible but at the acceptance floor.

hypothesis: Assign duration-zero impressions a dedicated category so the FM can push these always-negative rows below genuinely short videos within each user.
expected_delta_basis: The card range is 0.001–0.004 and Fact 3 provides deterministic mechanism evidence, but only about 1.9% of rows are affected, so a conservative lower-third estimate is appropriate.

rejected_alternative.reason: The explicit unknown-duration flag is cheaper and isolates a deterministic signal before adding many sparse crossed categories.

change_summary: Compute duration quantiles from positive durations only and encode duration_ms == 0 as a dedicated UNK0 category.

reasons: No leakage or contract issue; validation labels are used only for evaluation, and SMOKE_EPOCHS caps training.
Change is isolated to positive-duration quantiles plus a dedicated zero-duration category; expected +0.0015 is plausible but below the 0.002 acceptance/noise floor.

Last generation had no child nodes, so there are no GAUC or nDCG@5 component deltas to diagnose.
Most informative next probe: within-user BPR pairwise loss, targeting ranking-loss alignment; Fact 7 shows 57.8% of valid users are discriminative.
This tests whether GAUC improves while nDCG@5 stays flat, which would indicate unresolved top-of-list ordering.
Validation-overfitting risk is currently low but will grow with repeated probing: non-improving streak 0 and zero sub-0.002 “wins” accepted.

plan.hypothesis: Combining seven-day recency weighting with within-user BPR will emphasize recent positive-negative preferences and improve transfer under drift more than recency-weighted pointwise training.
plan.reason: The original pointwise result was weak but positive and uncertain (mean delta +0.00036, SE 0.00024); BPR is now the champion and changes which historical rows and pairs drive ranking gradients.

plan.hypothesis: Sampling three same-user negatives per positive will reduce wasted updates on already-correct pairs and improve GAUC and top-list ordering over single-negative BPR.

hypothesis: Combining seven-day recency weighting with BPR should emphasize recent within-user preference pairs and transfer better under temporal drift than recency-weighted pointwise training.
expected_delta_basis: Node_002 was weak but positive at +0.0005 on pointwise FM, while Data Fact 5 documents strong traffic and label drift, so a changed BPR parent justifies a low-cost retest.

rejected_alternative.reason: Its isolated pointwise test was negative (-0.0003), whereas recency was positive and has a clearer interaction with the changed BPR loss.

change_summary: Add normalized seven-day recency weights and scale each BPR pair gradient by the mean weight of its positive and sampled negative rows.

reasons: No leakage or unauthorized data access; outcomes are used only as training labels.
The change is isolated and contract-compliant, though the expected +0.0008 is below the 0.002 noise floor and requires multi-seed interpretation.

hypothesis: Sampling three uniform same-user negatives per positive should spend more updates on informative ordering errors and improve both GAUC and top-list ranking over single-negative BPR.
expected_delta_basis: The card range is 0.000–0.004, and node_001's +0.0026 GAUC but only +0.0007 nDCG indicates room to refine pair sampling, though calibration places a first attempt in the range's lower third.

rejected_alternative.reason: It targets the same loss component and cannot coexist in this generation; three-negative BPR is cheaper and fills the Consolidator's requested exploration slot.

change_summary: Expand each positive into three uniformly sampled same-user negative pairs per epoch, averaging all 3B pair gradients in one Adam step per original-positive batch.

reasons: Flattening all pairs creates 3x as many Adam updates, confounding multi-negative averaging with a larger optimization budget and stronger repeated regularization.
Expected +0.0013 is below the 0.002 noise floor, so a single-seed result is inconclusive.
critic.instructions: Batch original positives, sample three negatives per positive, repeat each positive only inside that batch, average gradients over the resulting 3B pairs, and perform one Adam step per original-positive batch. Confirm any sub-0.002 result across at least three seeds.

reasons: No leakage or contract violation; three negatives are sampled uniformly within user and averaged in one update per original-positive batch.
Expected delta 0.0013 is below the 0.002 noise/acceptance floor, so any apparent sub-threshold gain needs at least three seeds.

hypothesis: Increasing embedding L2 to 1e-5 should reduce the clear post-epoch-8 overfitting of BPR while preserving its personalized ordering signal.
expected_delta_basis: The card range is 0.000–0.004, and the champion declines steadily from 0.6031 at epoch 8 to 0.6020 at epoch 12, providing direct evidence that modest regularization may help.

rejected_alternative.reason: EMA has a similarly small expected range but requires more implementation and can lag the rapidly improving early BPR epochs; a one-parameter L2 probe is cheaper.

change_summary: Increase only the FM embedding-vector L2 coefficient from 1e-6 to 1e-5 while keeping W regularization at 1e-6 and leaving BPR training unchanged.

reasons: The shared l2 now regularizes both embeddings V and linear biases W, while the hypothesis claims an embedding-only L2 change.
Expected delta 0.0012 is below the 0.002 acceptance/noise floor.
critic.instructions: Keep W regularization at the parent value 1e-6 and apply 1e-5 only to V; otherwise preserve the parent script exactly. Treat any apparent gain as inconclusive unless it reaches 0.002 or is confirmed across seeds.

reasons: No leakage or contract violation; valid long_view is used only for evaluation, and SMOKE_EPOCHS caps training.
Scope is limited to V L2=1e-5 while W remains 1e-6; expected +0.0012 is below the 0.002 floor, so only a >=0.002 gain or multi-seed confirmation is meaningful.

hypothesis: Leakage-safe per-user historical rates by author, tab, and duration bucket should add row-varying personalization beyond BPR's user-item interactions, particularly for sparse users.

hypothesis: Weighting BPR pairs by their current nDCG@5 swap impact should focus updates on top-ranked mistakes and convert the observed nDCG-specific movement into a larger primary gain.

rejected_alternative.reason: Checkpoint averaging addresses variance and mild overfitting but does not target the diagnosed top-5 ordering error and has a lower expected ceiling.

change_summary: Add LambdaRank nDCG@5 swap-impact weighting to sampled BPR pairs after one plain-BPR warm-up epoch.

reasons: No leakage or test access; labels are used only for training pairs and loss weights.
